clue.text: Flashy sort of vessel ?

parts.note: a boat that flashes a beam to warn passing ships, anchored where a lighthouse cannot stand

explanation.surface: A showy, glamorous boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flashy' suggests showiness, but the vessel really does flash: it carries a warning lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A moored boat carrying a beacon to guide shipping is exactly a vessel that flashes.

clue.text: Female worker was relieved

definitions.note: stands for the place that was relieved, not the verb

parts.note: a lady is a female
a smith is a metal worker

explanation.surface: A woman labourer feels relief.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a historical fact: Ladysmith, in South Africa, was besieged in the Boer War and relieved in 1900.
explanation.definitionFit: The Natal town besieged by the Boers for four months was famously relieved by British forces in February 1900.

clue.text: A gift from Ulysses ?

definitions.meaning: Ulysses S. ... was a US general and president

explanation.definitionFit: A grant is money given; Ulysses S. Grant led the Union army in the American Civil War.

clue.text: Wrong river to find this creature .

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
the Oise is a river in northern France

explanation.surface: A creature discovered at the wrong river.
explanation.walkthrough: TORT is the legal word for a civil wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoise is a slow land reptile with a domed shell, a creature.

clue.text: Pianist brings nothing into German port

indicators.note: into puts the letter for nothing inside the port

parts.note: Hamburg is Germany's chief port
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A pianist arrives empty-handed at a German port.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Hambourg was a Russian-born British concert pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Hambourg (1879-1960) was a celebrated concert pianist of his day.

clue.text: Pictures found in separating some litter

indicators.note: separating means the word in splits the pups apart

parts.note: pups make up a litter of young dogs

explanation.surface: Photos discovered among the young of a litter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a link but the letters IN, which are 'separating' PUPS into P and UPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pin-ups are pictures of attractive people pinned to a wall.

clue.text: Strokes made in set by way of return

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

indicators.note: return asks for the abbreviation for way to be read backwards

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Strokes executed in a set as the ball comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like a tennis set, but it is the verb; 'way' is the street abbreviation, turned round by 'of return'.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf green, the gentle strokes that roll the ball towards the hole are its putts.

clue.text: Mountain rises in southern steppes

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word for mountain is read upwards

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

explanation.surface: A mountain towers over the southern grasslands.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rises' means read from the bottom up; 'in' is not a link but letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Steppes are vast treeless grasslands, flat open country.

clue.text: Easily managed vehicle is back on list

indicators.note: is back means the word for vehicle runs backwards

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle
a table is a list of figures

explanation.surface: A car that is easy to handle is back on the register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is back' sits beside 'vehicle', so only that word is turned; the list is a table of figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractable animal or person is docile and readily controlled.

clue.text: Lover was awkward at home

indicators.note: awkward signals the letters of was are clumsily rearranged

parts.note: someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A lover behaved clumsily at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges WAS into SWA.
explanation.definitionFit: A swain is an old poetic word for a young suitor.

clue.text: Indian city shown in obscure plan

indicators.note: in places the city inside the word for obscure

parts.note: dim means obscure or murky
Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: An Indian city marked on a murky map.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a drawn plan or outline showing how something is laid out.

clue.text: Falls for a redhead once more in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of red
once more means again

explanation.surface: Someone falls in love with a red-haired woman again after retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' turns the whole run A + R + AGAIN backwards, giving the falls; 'redhead' gives only R, the first letter of red.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous waterfall on the US-Canada border, so the clue's falls name it.

clue.text: The fight in Barset town hall ?

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words Barset town

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out in the town hall of Trollope's Barchester county.
explanation.walkthrough: Barset is Trollope's fictional county; the fight is found inside 'Barset town'.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief, sharp quarrel or scrap.

clue.text: Kent town provides replacement for G.P. in Troon

indicators.note: a replacement rearranges the letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters G and P as printed
taken as written
taken as written, the Scottish golfing town

explanation.surface: A doctor in Troon is replaced by one from a Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' shuffles GP IN TROON into the Kent town; G.P. looks like a family doctor, Troon a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpington is a town on the London-Kent border, historically in Kent and famous for its chickens.

clue.text: Eastern religious types 'ave a go, with diligence

indicators.note: the dropped H of have shows the H must fall from the word for the believers

parts.note: Hindus follow the chief religion of India, in the East
a try is a go or attempt

explanation.surface: Cockney-voiced followers of an Eastern faith have a try, working hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ave is have with its H dropped, telling the solver to drop the H of HINDUS too, leaving INDUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry in its older sense is steady hard work, diligence.

clue.text: Hundred tales of French romance, possibly

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: possibly shows that romance is only one arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: A hundred French love stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ROMANCE into CAMERON; the Decameron is in fact Italian, by Boccaccio.
explanation.definitionFit: Boccaccio's Decameron is a collection of a hundred stories told over ten days.

clue.text: Come up against an objection

parts.note: a but is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Raising a quibble.
explanation.definitionFit: Two properties that abut touch along a boundary, meeting up against each other.

clue.text: A conveyance, or an accolade?

definitions.meaning: a document transferring ownership of land
dubbing a knight, the accolade, is the act that gives a title

explanation.definitionFit: A deed proving ownership of property; an accolade is literally a deed that confers a title.

clue.text: Control of course needed for such passengers

definitions.meaning: ... passengers travelled in the cheapest quarters

explanation.definitionFit: Steering a vessel is one sense; the cheap class of passenger berths is the other.

clue.text: Oust from the underworld, perhaps

definitions.meaning: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, so his place is the underworld

explanation.definitionFit: Displace means push out; split, it is Dis place, home of the Roman underworld god.

clue.text: Cut work of poor writer'?

definitions.meaning: ... work is dull writing done for money by a drudge

explanation.definitionFit: Chop roughly is one sense; the other is the jobbing scribbler's dull output.

clue.text: Direction to aircraft appears harsh

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction
the Trident was a British airliner of the 1960s

explanation.surface: An order to a plane sounds harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direction to aircraft' reads as an air-traffic instruction, but it is S (south) followed by the Trident, a Hawker Siddeley airliner.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice or sound is loud, grating and unpleasant.

clue.text: Sayings in yearly letters to The Times ?

parts.note: AD, anno domini, are the letters placed with years
ages are times, long periods

explanation.surface: Proverbs in the annual correspondence to a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is the newspaper in the surface; here it means ages, eras.
explanation.definitionFit: Adages are old proverbs, traditional sayings.

clue.text: Compose a feature, film?

definitions.meaning: a cosmetic film laid over a facial feature

explanation.definitionFit: Make up means compose; cosmetics coat the face in a thin layer, the other sense.

clue.text: Means to be in time to change without delay

indicators.note: to be in says the word for means sits inside the other letters
change tells us to rearrange the letters of time

parts.note: media are means of communication

explanation.surface: Someone intends to arrive punctually so as to change at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' looks like a verb, intends, but it is the noun, channels of communication; 'to change' signals the anagram of 'time', and 'to be in' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An immediate response comes at once, with no pause or waiting.

clue.text: Drive for a mile, roughly, round Polish capital

indicators.note: round shows the jumbled letters go around the capital letter
roughly tells us the letters of mile are jumbled
capital means the first letter of Polish

explanation.surface: A mile's journey around the Polish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' turns MILE into IMEL, and 'round' wraps it about P, the 'capital' of Polish; Warsaw is the false lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push forward.

clue.text: Race course supporter?

definitions.meaning: a ... is a horse race whose prize was once a silver ...
a dinner ... holds up each course of a meal

explanation.definitionFit: A Plate is a horse race; a dish bearing each course of dinner is the other sense.

clue.text: A high room for us jolly sailor-boys

definitions.note: points to the sailors' word for up in the rigging

parts.note: a loft is a room high under the roof

explanation.surface: An attic for us cheerful sailors, as in a sea shanty.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the sailors' setting: aloft is where a seaman climbs, up the masts and rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloft is nautical talk for up in the rigging, where sailors work.

clue.text: Sanctimonious rascal in canoe

parts.note: pi is a slang shortening of pious, sanctimonious
a rogue is a rascal

explanation.surface: A self-righteous scoundrel paddles off in a canoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirogue is a dugout canoe used in the Caribbean and Louisiana.

clue.text: Sea-food for Jack only. ?

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, abbreviated AB, able seaman
alone means only

explanation.surface: Seafood meant just for Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a sailor, so AB (able seaman).
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is an edible sea snail, prized as a shellfish delicacy.

clue.text: Wrinkles the bride gets after marriage.

definitions.meaning: marriage ... are the certificate a bride is handed after the wedding

explanation.definitionFit: Facial creases are one sense; marriage lines, the certificate, the other.

clue.text: Quietly took umbrage, being introduced

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
to take umbrage is to resent

explanation.surface: Someone silently bristles at being introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest presented at court is being formally introduced.
